subject: Console + API onboarding: seat allocation and demo swap request
messages:
From: Alex Mercado <alex@finbridge.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@finbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: swap APAC evening seats + clarify sandbox limits

Hey Sergio —

Quick one from our side. We originally booked the Tuesday afternoon slot (US hours) for our cross-region onboarding, but we realized a bunch of our APAC engineers need to attend live. Would Redwood be open to swapping that seat allocation so APAC evening (your local morning) covers the demo and the US team can join the recording?

Two asks:
- Can you confirm how many simultaneous console seats are available for the live demo (we have ~18 people, but only ~8 need seat-level access)?
- For the API enablement, does the sandbox support token-per-client segmentation? We want to make sure we can test multi-tenant request patterns during the canary session.

Attaching our onboarding checklist and attendee matrix.

If possible, propose an APAC-friendly evening window next week (UTC+5:30 / +8 windows).

Appreciate it —
Alex
Head of Integrations
FinBridge

Attachment: FinBridge_onboard_requirements.pdf

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercado <alex@finbridge.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: swap APAC evening seats + clarify sandbox limits

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the matrix. Camila (on enablement) and Ben (ops) are looped for capacity and runbook details.

Short answers up front:
- Console seats: we can provision up to 25 observer seats in the live demo environment and grant 10 interactive seats (keyboard/API keys) without extra configuration. If you need more than 10 interaction seats we can enable additional seats for the session — give us a headcount and we’ll add them.
- Sandbox segmentation: yes — we can issue per-client API keys and isolate KV caches per key so your multi-tenant patterns are reproducible during the canary tests. There are rate limits per key (default 60 rpm) which we can raise temporarily for the hands-on lab.

Proposed APAC-friendly windows (pick one):
- Mon 23 Nov 2026, 18:30–20:00 SGT (UTC+8)
- Tue 24 Nov 2026, 19:00–20:30 IST (UTC+5:30) — good if most are India-based
- Wed 25 Nov 2026, 17:00–18:30 SGT (backup)

Camila: I attached our runbook v2 (redwood_onboard-runbook-v2.pdf) — can you confirm the preflight steps and whether we should seed any sample prompts or flows for FinBridge?

Ben: can you prep a short canary checklist (token limits, KV cache warmup, fallback policy) — I’ll attach it to the calendar invite.

If any of those windows look good to you we’ll send a calendar invite + Zoom and provision the extra seats.

— Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_onboard-runbook-v2.pdf

From: Alex Mercado <alex@finbridge.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@finbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 01:22:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: Request: swap APAC evening seats + clarify sandbox limits

Thanks — Mon 23 Nov 18:30 SGT works best for us. We confirmed final attendee list: 16 live attendees, 6 will need interactive access (devs), the rest observers. We also want a short canary session at the start to run our sensitive PII-scrubbing flow against the sandbox before the main demo. Two small asks:

1) Can the per-client API keys be flagged so logs are tagged with "finbridge-canary" for the first 15 minutes? We want to make it easy for our security team to scan;
2) Will you be able to increase the per-key rpm to 200 for the canary window? We’ll only run a burst for 10 minutes.

If you can confirm those items we’ll approve the swap and I’ll share the attendee names this afternoon.

— Alex

Zoom + calendar: I created the event and attached the runbook and the canary checklist. Calendar invite (will come from camila_reyes@redwood.com) includes: Zoom link, API key coordination doc, and the short runbook.
